text: Thank you for sharing that history. To better understand your condition, could you describe the specific nature of the discomfort you feel during sexual activity, and how long have you been experiencing difficulty conceiving?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of body dysmorphic disorder and the description of pelvic floor muscle tension, have you tried any pelvic floor physical therapy or Kegel exercises to address this discomfort? Additionally, would you be willing to undergo a pelvic exam or imaging to rule out structural causes like endometriosis or adhesions? REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to vaginismus with concurrent pelvic floor hypertonicity, in the setting of unexplained infertility and male erectile dysfunction.
